note: EXAMPLE manifest for a REAL Stage-1 pretraining corpus. Use it (or copy its entries into datasets/v2/manifest.json) with 'tinymind data prepare-corpus --manifest datasets/v2/corpus.manifest.example.json --out data/corpus --allow-download', or set the train-50m workflow inputs dataset_manifest=datasets/v2/corpus.manifest.example.json and allow_download=true. Shards are streamed one at a time into a download cache under the output directory (never into git), hashed while streaming, verified against 'sha256' when given, chunked, deduplicated across the whole corpus (repeated paragraphs, exact and MinHash near-duplicate chunks), split deterministically into train/val/test by document group, and recorded with source, license, redacted URL, per-shard SHA-256, token counts, the tokenizer hash and this manifest's hash in corpus_manifest.json. PINNING: the first preparation records every shard's observed sha256 in corpus_manifest.json; copy those values into 'sha256' (one per shard, same order) so later runs refuse silently changed data. PRIVATE DATA: add "auth_env": "HF_TOKEN" (Hugging Face gated/private datasets) or "auth_env": "CORPUS_TOKEN" (any other bearer-token host) to an entry and create the repository secret of that name; train-50m.yml passes those two secrets to the data-preparation step only (never to training). The token is sent only to the shard's own host, never forwarded on a redirect, and never logged or recorded. LOCAL DATA: a 'local' entry takes file paths (relative to this file), absolute paths or file:// URLs, e.g. {"source": "my_books", "type": "local", "format": "text", "shards": ["/data/books/part-000.txt.gz", "/data/books/part-001.txt.gz"], "license": "..."}. SIZE: keep chunk_chars x tokens-per-character + 2 within the model's max_seq_len (about 4 characters per token for a 16k BPE; 1 per token for the byte tokenizer); max_records caps the chunks kept from a source and is spread evenly over its shards (at most ceil(max_records / shards) from each). The same manifest format serves every model size: a 500M or 1B run lists more shards (and, for a corpus deduplicated upstream, can prepare with --dedup exact).
